title: The Beaver Harris album, 1975
summary: Beaver Harris, from Homestead, asked her to sing two songs on his 360 Degree Music Experience album; she sings 'Can There Be Peace'.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Right. Okay. Well, now we come to 1975. And this is a productive year for you in terms of albums, anyway, because you're on four records in this year.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
How about that?
And the first one is the one that I didn't know about until you showed me recently. And I was quite astounded when I saw your name on the cover of a Beaver Harris album.
Oh, yeah!
That was in either January or February of 1975.
Yes. I had done a gig up in Connecticut for Bill Ratzenberger. And Beaver Harris was on drums. And it turned out that Beaver Harris was also from Pittsburgh, so it was --
Yes, he played with -- in fact, he played on the Homestead baseball team.

That's right. And, of course, I mean Beaver is much younger than I am. I don't remember Beaver from Pittsburgh. But anyway, we had a long conversation, and we discussed quite a few things. And, of course,
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Beaver Harris has this group, the Three Hundred and Sixty Degree Musical Experience.
So they had a record date and he wrote two songs, and asked me to sing them. And I did these two -- 'Can There Be Peace' and 'I Wish I Knew.'
So, we do have copies of that album.
And that was made in February of 1975 with Herb Hall on clarinet, Doc Cheatham on trumpet, Marshall Brown on valve trombone, Dave Gurrell on piano, Jimmy Garrison, and Beaver Harris on drums.
Marshall made these arrangements.
It's an interesting juxtaposition of old-timers, shall we say--without being pejorative---
Yes.
On the wind instruments and they're on the modern rhythm sections.
Yes.
But it works very nicely, and your voice is in top form.
Well --
'Can There Be Peace,' I think, is one of your very best performances.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
I haven't done those things at all since date. And I wasn't too sure that I had done justice to his songs, but I'm glad to hear you say 'Can There Be Peace' turned out pretty good.
Well, I don't know. Maybe this is my own kind of personal bias and prejudice, and so on.
You know, it was all right. I mean, I like to hear --
(Inaudible).

I don't know whether that many people heard it not. I have not heard any reaction from the album. I don't think that these guys actually worked together except on that particular date. Because Herb Hall and Doc Cheatham and Marshall, they're all on their own. And, of course, there were a lot of other young musicians on the session that day. They did other tunes which way over my head. They were way out!
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Well, I think that's the intent.
Yeah. Well he says from ragtime to no time -- whatever that means.
What I meant before is that I personally seemed to be attractive to the more dirge-like song --
Yeah. I liked it. I mean, I sang it. I mean, I enjoyed it.
That may be a person idiosyncrasy of mine, but I find that and the one I mentioned before on the Shakespeare album --
Come (inaudible).
